purpose: Controlled validation pack for first human reviewer calibration and first human-reviewed NDS proof packet.

selection_rules.notes: Balanced first-pass NDS validation pack intended for calibration and proof, not full-scale production benchmarking.

cases.title: No clear starting point, afraid of sounding ordinary
cases.student_input_raw: I really do not know what to write about. Nothing in my life feels dramatic or special, and I am scared my essay will sound boring.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student has blank-page paralysis and believes their life lacks a dramatic or obviously impressive story. Needs direction toward a specific, authentic narrative center.

cases.title: Many possible memories, no selection logic
cases.student_input_raw: I have a bunch of random moments I could maybe write about, but I cannot tell which one actually matters for an essay.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student has candidate memories but lacks narrative-selection logic. Needs help identifying which moment reveals interpretive identity rather than random anecdote.

context.notes: Tests selection logic rather than total absence of ideas.

cases.title: Strong resume, no narrative center
cases.student_input_raw: I have robotics, soccer, volunteering, debate, and an internship, but I do not know which one to focus on or if I should combine them.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student presents multiple high-signal activities but no narrative center. Needs direction away from resume breadth and toward a coherent interpretive story.

cases.title: Leadership overload becoming generic
cases.student_input_raw: Everyone tells me to write about leadership because I held leadership roles, but that feels like what everyone else is probably doing too.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is being pushed toward a generic leadership framing and senses the risk. Needs help distinguishing real narrative value from common prestige framing.

cases.title: Identity instinct without a concrete story
cases.student_input_raw: I feel like my background matters a lot to who I am, but I do not know how to write about identity without sounding broad or cliché.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student feels identity is central but lacks a concrete narrative angle. Needs help narrowing from abstract identity language to lived, specific interpretation.

cases.title: Community belonging but no interpretive core
cases.student_input_raw: My community shaped me a lot, but when I try to explain that, it turns into a big general statement instead of an actual essay idea.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student has a community-based instinct but no specific interpretive center. Needs help moving from diffuse belonging language to a precise narrative direction.

cases.title: Family hardship topic uncertainty
cases.student_input_raw: Something difficult happened in my family and it changed me a lot, but I do not know if writing about it would feel honest or like I am trying to use it for admissions.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is considering a sensitive family hardship topic and is conflicted about authenticity versus performative use. Needs guidance on whether and how this could be handled.

cases.title: Personal difficulty but unsure if too heavy
cases.student_input_raw: I went through something personal that definitely affected me, but I do not know if it is too serious or too risky to center an essay on it.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is weighing a personal difficulty topic but is uncertain about tone, risk, and strategic fit. Needs careful direction rather than encouragement by default.

cases.title: Service trip essay temptation
cases.student_input_raw: One of my first ideas was writing about how a service trip changed my perspective, but now I am worried that sounds like the most predictable essay possible.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is drawn to a potentially overused transformational service-trip frame and already suspects genericness risk. Needs sharper direction toward specificity or an alternative angle.

cases.title: Sports injury comeback cliché risk
cases.student_input_raw: I could write about recovering from an injury in my sport, but I know comeback essays can sound very standard. I do not know if mine is actually different.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student has a common adversity/comeback topic and needs help determining whether there is a distinctive interpretive angle or whether the topic should be redirected.

context.notes: Tests differentiation under common topic pressure.

cases.title: High-achievement path but unclear deepest story
cases.student_input_raw: I am good at a lot of school-related things, but I do not know what actually sounds most like me instead of just what looks strong on paper.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is asking for a direction that fits who they are, not just what appears impressive. Needs a strong student-fit read and anti-prestige filtering.

cases.title: Parents pushing one angle, student unsure
cases.student_input_raw: My parents think I should write about the hardest thing I have done, but I am not sure that is actually the best way to show who I am.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is receiving external pressure toward one essay direction but is uncertain whether it reflects their real best narrative angle. Needs strong student-fit judgment.

cases.title: Choosing what sounds impressive
cases.student_input_raw: Part of me wants to choose the topic that sounds the most impressive to top schools, even if it is not the one that feels most natural.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is explicitly prestige-optimizing and needs redirection toward authentic strategic differentiation rather than status signaling.

cases.title: List of activities presented as essay content
cases.student_input_raw: Here are the main things I have done: student council, debate captain, volunteer tutoring, NHS, piano, and internship experience. Which one is the best essay topic?
cases.student_input_normalized: Student provides a resume-like list and asks for topic selection. Needs help reframing from activity inventory to actual narrative and interpretive value.

cases.title: Wants something unusual but also safe
cases.student_input_raw: I want my essay to stand out and feel unique, but I also do not want to take any risks or choose something that could be misunderstood.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student wants both distinctiveness and total safety, creating contradictory strategic pressure. Needs balanced direction rather than false certainty.

cases.title: Cultural background matters but feels overgeneralized
cases.student_input_raw: My cultural background definitely matters to me, but every time I try to explain it, it feels like I am making broad statements instead of saying something real.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student wants to write about cultural background but cannot yet locate a lived, specific narrative angle. Needs narrowing and grounding.

cases.title: Mental-health adjacent caution without explicit diagnosis
cases.student_input_raw: There was a period where I was really struggling internally and it changed how I see everything now, but I do not know if that is something I should even bring into an essay.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is describing a sensitive internal struggle without giving clinical detail. Needs careful direction on whether an adjacent or more controlled angle is stronger.

cases.title: Too many strong angles causing paralysis
cases.student_input_raw: My problem is not that I have no ideas. My problem is that I have too many things I could write about and they all seem equally valid.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student has many potentially viable directions and needs prioritization logic, not idea generation.

cases.title: Strong story candidate but unsure if too small
cases.student_input_raw: There is one smaller personal story that feels very me, but I keep wondering if it is too small compared to bigger, more impressive things I could write about.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student senses a high-fit story but doubts its scale relative to more visibly impressive options. Needs help distinguishing significance from spectacle.

cases.title: Essay idea sounds polished but empty
cases.student_input_raw: I can make a topic sound polished and meaningful when I talk about it, but I am worried it is more polished than real.
cases.student_input_normalized: Student is aware of the risk of constructing a polished but hollow essay frame. Needs guidance toward substance over rhetorical smoothness.
